Is there some list out there recording logical errors first discovered during the formalization process? I’m guessing there are very few big theorems that were thought to be true and later disproved during the formalization process, but what about smaller lemmas and other proof steps that turned out to be invalid?

And then a related but distinct question: is there some list recording instances where the formalization process elucidated the need for some non-trivial lemmas that were never present in the original natural language proof? I think this is probably harder to define since non-trivial isn’t exactly a rigorous terms.

Oren Hartstein said:

the need for some non-trivial lemmas that were never present in the original natural language proof

This is usually called "invisible mathematics" by Emily Riehl, see these for examples:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJfoqKDenpw
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0_N1fnaagrs

I like the very easy but non-trivial docs#SimpleGraph.Walk.exists_boundary_dart which is usually part of handwaving arguments without actually proving it (much like other "obvious from the picture" arguments)
